final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest phenotype score (0.997); Cys39 is a RING zinc ligand, so Ser abolishes Zn binding and RING/BARD1 E3 function with only local perturbation, preserving overall folding.
Score 0.990 on Zn-coordinating Cys61; a classic pathogenic variant that disrupts RING E3 ligase activity while the polypeptide remains folded.
Score 0.973; second Zn-coordinating cysteine in the RING domain, same validated LOF mechanism with minimal misfolding risk, slightly lower score than C39S/C61G.

stop_reason.detail: Aligned phenotype evidence is saturated for the top candidates; additional tools add little decision value.

history.rationale: C61 is a zinc-coordinating cysteine in the N-terminal RING finger; its disruption abolishes E3 ligase function and BRCA1-BARD1 heterodimer stability, a classic pathogenic LOF variant.
RING-domain zinc-coordinating cysteine (C61) in the BARD1-interaction interface; mutation is a classic LOF driver disrupting ubiquitin ligase function while preserving fold.
AlphaMissense 0.990 on the RING Zn-coordinating Cys61; known to abolish E3 ligase activity and BARD1 interaction while leaving the global polypeptide fold intact.
Second zinc-ligand cysteine in the RING domain; substitution destroys the fold-local zinc binding and protein-protein interaction surface required for repair.
Second RING zinc ligand; known pathogenic variant class that abolishes BRCA1 E3 activity with minimal global misfolding.
Score 0.973; second Zn-coordinating cysteine in the RING, classic LOF mechanism, retained as strong backup.
Well-characterized pathogenic BRCT-domain variant; disrupts hydrophobic core packing of the C-terminal BRCT repeat and phosphopeptide recognition.
Well-documented BRCT-domain pathogenic mutation disrupting phosphopeptide recognition.
Well-documented BRCT pathogenic variant; AlphaMissense 0.893 is the lowest of the pool but supported by strong literature prior, slightly demoted.
Pathogenic BRCT missense variant; serine in the BRCT hydrophobic core replaced by bulky phenylalanine impairs BRCT folding and function.
BRCT1 pocket residue implicated in pSer binding; bulky aromatic substitution expected to abolish ligand binding.
Score 0.894 at the BRCT coiled-coil interface; retains value but below the leading candidates.
Known pathogenic BRCT-core substitution; introducing a charged glutamate into a buried alanine destabilizes the BRCT fold and abolishes DNA-damage response function.
BRCT interface residue known from cancer databases as pathogenic; charge introduction disrupts BRCT tandem packing.
Score 0.971 in the BRCT phospho-binding pocket; expected to disrupt BRCT-mediated interactions; keeps domain diversity in the pool.
H41 participates in RING zinc coordination; proline substitution likely disrupts local geometry and RING stability.
RING-domain adjacent residue; plausible disruption of zinc-coordination geometry.
Score 0.989 in the RING domain; proline insertion is strongly disruptive locally, supporting LOF, with modest risk to overall folding only.
C39 is a RING zinc-coordinating cysteine; Cys-to-Ser substitution weakens zinc ligation and destabilizes the RING domain.
Another zinc-coordinating cysteine in RING; serine substitution a milder but validated LOF route.
Highest phenotype score (0.997); Cys39 is a RING zinc ligand, so Ser substitution destroys Zn binding and RING function with only local structural perturbation.
Proline at BRCT hydrophobic interface; charged arginine substitution is a documented pathogenic variant disrupting BRCT packing.
Conserved proline in BRCT2; substitution likely distorts the phospho-binding cleft.
Score 0.941 in BRCT2; known pathogenic hotspot region, retained as BRCT alternative.
